source:
πρόσωπον ὃ ἐνεδύσατο, τίς ἱκανὸς ἐλέγξαι; τίς ἱκανὸς ἀποκαλύψαι καὶ δεῖξαι ὅ τι
ἔνδον δράκων ἐστί; Καὶ μετ' ὀλίγα. Πρὸς τὴν μνήμην ἀνέ δραμον τῶν ἱερῶν
γραμμάτων, τούτῳ θεοπ νεύστῳ βιβλίῳ τοῦ Ἰὼβ ἐγκειμένων, καὶ ὡς ἐν σωματικῇ
διαπλάσει τὸ λίαν ἀνειδὲς καὶ ποικίλον κεκρυμμένον τῶν ἐπινοιῶν καὶ τῆς τῶν
ἔξωθεν προσωπείων ἀπαλλαγῆς, ἀπο γράφων τοῦ διαβόλου καὶ δαιμόνων ἀρχε
κάκου καὶ πονηρῶν. Φησὶ γάρ· Τίς ἀποκαλύ ψει πρόσωπον ἐνδύσεως αὐτοῦ; –Καὶ
ἐπεί περ ἔριζε τῆς ἔξωθεν φαινομένης ταύτης ποικιλίας, ὡς ἔκ τινος βάθους τῆς
ἀφανοῦς κακίας ἀνίσχουσι, ἐπενήνεκται τοῖς εἰρη μένοις καὶ ταῦτα· Τίς ἀποκαλύψει
πρόσωπον ἐνδύσεως αὐτοῦ, τουτέστι τίς ἱκανὸς εἰσελ θεῖν εἰς τὰ νοήματα τῆς
καρδίας αὐτοῦ, διότι συνεπτυγμένα τυγχάνουσι; ιδʹ, ιεʹ, Οὐ σαλευθήσεται, ἡ καρδία
αὐτοῦ 388 πέπηγεν ὡς λίθος, ἕστηκεν δὲ ὥσπερ ἄκ μων ἀνήλατος. Ἀπελιθώθη,
φησὶν, ἡ καρδία αὐτοῦ, καὶ οὐκ ἐλαθῆναι δύναται· ἀλλ' ὅλος ἐστὶν ἀπεσ κληκὼς καὶ
ἰταμός· οὐκ ἐλαυνόμενος, οὐκ ἀκολουθῶν λόγῳ, οὐκ εἴκει· ὁ δὲ σκληρός ἐστιν,
ἀνήλατος, ἀνένδοτος. Καὶ εἴ τις ἀπὸ τοῦ διαβόλου ἀπέσπασε δύναμιν, καὶ τού του
δράκοντος αὐτὸς ἔχει τὴν καρδίαν ἀνή λατον καὶ οὐκ ἐλαυνομένην. Εἰ δέ τις χρυσός
ἐστιν ἀκολουθῶν τῷ λόγῳ, τῷ χρυσοχοϊκῷ οὗτος εἴκει ἕως ἂν γένηται πέταλον
χρυσοῦν, καὶ δέξηται τοὺς τύπους τῶν γραμμάτων τοῦ Θεοῦ, ἐν Χριστῷ Ἰησοῦ, ᾧ ἡ
δόξα εἰς τοὺς αἰῶνας αἰώνων. Ἀμήν. Κεφ. ΜΒʹ, ιʹ. Ἔδωκεν δὲ ὁ Κύριος διπλᾶ ὅσα ἦν
ἔμπροσθεν Ἰὼβ εἰς διπλασιασμόν. ιβʹ. Ὁ δὲ Κύριος εὐλόγησε τὰ ἔσχατα Ἰὼβ, ἢ τὰ
ἔμπροσθεν· ἦν δὲ τὰ κτήνην αὐ τοῦ, πρόβατα μύρια τετρακισχίλια, κάμη λοι
ἐξακισχίλιαι, ζεύγη βοῶν χίλια. ιγʹ. Γεννῶνται δὲ αὐτῷ υἱοὶ ἑπτὰ καὶ θυ γατέρες
τρεῖς.
english: The face he put on—who is able to expose it? Who is able to uncover it and show what is inside: that it is a dragon? (And a little further on) I ran back to the memory of the sacred writings contained in this divinely inspired book of Job, and as in a bodily shaping, the exceedingly formless and varied thing hidden from his thoughts and from the putting off of outward masks, describing the devil, source of evil, and wicked demons. For he says: “Who will uncover the face of his garment?” (Job 41:4 LXX). And since he was contending about this outward visible variety, as if from some depth of unseen vice they rise up, these words have also been added to what was said: “Who will uncover the face of his garment?”—that is, who is able to enter into the thoughts of his heart, because they are folded together? “His heart will not be shaken; it is fixed like stone, and it stands like an anvil that cannot be driven” (Job 41:5-6 LXX). His heart, he says, has been turned to stone, and it cannot be driven; but he is wholly hardened and bold—not driven, not following reason, not yielding. But the hard one is unbeaten, unyielding. And if anyone has torn away power from the devil, this dragon himself still has the heart, unbeaten and not driven. But if anyone is gold following the word, this one yields to the goldsmith until he becomes a golden leaf and receives the impressions of the letters of God, in Christ Jesus, to whom be glory forever and ever. Amen. Chapter 42, verse 10. “And the Lord gave double all that belonged to Job before, for a doubling” (Job 42:10). Verse 12. “And the Lord blessed the last things of Job, or the former things; and his livestock were fourteen thousand sheep, six thousand camels, a thousand yoke of oxen” (Job 42:12). Verse 13. “And there were born to him seven sons and three daughters” (Job 42:13).

findings.quote: the exceedingly formless and varied thing hidden from his thoughts and from the putting off of outward masks
findings.source_quote: τὸ λίαν ἀνειδὲς καὶ ποικίλον κεκρυμμένον τῶν ἐπινοιῶν καὶ τῆς τῶν ἔξωθεν προσωπείων ἀπαλλαγῆς
findings.checker_says: ἀπαλλαγῆς means 'removal/escape from', not 'putting off of'; sense is 'hidden from thoughts and from removal of outward masks'
findings.reviewer_note: Catena sentence has no main verb and is likely corrupt; the English is murky but the proposed fix is no better grounded.

findings.quote: this dragon himself still has the heart, unbeaten and not driven
findings.source_quote: τούτου δράκοντος αὐτὸς ἔχει τὴν καρδίαν ἀνήλατον καὶ οὐκ ἐλαυνομένην
findings.checker_says: αὐτὸς ἔχει means 'he himself has', not 'this dragon himself still has the heart'; subject is the one who tore power from devil, not the dragon
findings.reviewer_note: τούτου δράκοντος is genitive with τὴν καρδίαν: whoever draws power from the devil has the dragon's heart. English makes the dragon the subject; 'torn away' earlier should be 'drawn'.

findings.quote: this dragon himself still has the heart, unbeaten and not driven
findings.source_quote: τούτου δράκοντος αὐτὸς ἔχει τὴν καρδίαν ἀνήλατον καὶ οὐκ ἐλαυνομένην
findings.checker_says: Re-reading: τούτου δράκοντος = 'of this dragon' (genitive); αὐτὸς ἔχει = 'he himself has'. The one who tore power from the devil—this dragon (genitive of specification/species)—he himself has the heart. Or: 'this dragon, he himself has...' English 'this dragon himself still has the heart' makes dragon the subject, but αὐτὸς is intensive 'he himself' referring to the subject of the conditional (τις). The sense is: even if someone tore power from the devil, this dragon-type person himself still has... Actually ambiguous. Let me re-parse: 'And if anyone has torn away power from the devil, and of this dragon, he himself has the heart...' Hmm, τούτου δράκοντος could be genitive absolute or apposition. I think English is wrong to make dragon the subject.
findings.reviewer_note: Duplicate of #1; proposed 'as for this dragon' keeps the wrong parse. ἀνήλατος = unmalleable (cf. the goldsmith image), so 'unbeaten' misleads.

findings.quote: describing the devil, source of evil, and wicked demons
findings.source_quote: ἀπογράφων τοῦ διαβόλου καὶ δαιμόνων ἀρχεκάκου καὶ πονηρῶν
findings.checker_says: ἀπογράφων is 'copying/describing from', but ἀρχεκάκου modifies devil (ἀρχέκακος = source of evil), not demons; syntax is 'of the devil, source of evil, and of wicked demons'
findings.reviewer_note: English already attaches 'source of evil' to the devil only; referee misread the English.

findings.quote: And the Lord blessed the last things of Job, or the former things
findings.source_quote: Ὁ δὲ Κύριος εὐλόγησε τὰ ἔσχατα Ἰὼβ, ἢ τὰ ἔμπροσθεν
findings.checker_says: ἢ here is 'than' (comparative), not 'or'; sense is 'blessed the last things of Job more than the former things'

findings.quote: And the Lord blessed the last things of Job, or the former things
findings.source_quote: Ὁ δὲ Κύριος εὐλόγησε τὰ ἔσχατα Ἰὼβ, ἢ τὰ ἔμπροσθεν
findings.checker_says: Confirmed: ἢ = 'than' in comparative blessing formula. 'Blessed the latter end of Job more than his beginning' (KJV). English 'or' is wrong.
